caption: Four months to the wedding and the deposit already ate a car payment. Did anyone's wedding actually come in on budget?

slides.title:
How we spend
our R36 000
planning our wedding
Living in Mahikeng
slides.body:
Him 27, her 26
Engaged, no kids yet
Jobs: Municipal library assistant & sales rep at a furniture store
Combined net: R36 000 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 2 bed townhouse, we moved in together in January
slides.body: We priced venues before we priced this place. The venue lost.

slides.title: Wedding savings
slides.includes: Joint account, no withdrawals until the date
slides.body: We picked the date first and worked backward. Eight months of this and we're still short.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Two of us, plus his mother most Sundays
slides.body: She comes for lunch and leaves with leftovers. We've stopped minding.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: Her car, his is paid off
slides.body: We argued about trading it in before the wedding. We're keeping it.

slides.title: Catering deposit
slides.includes: Paid this month, balance due a month before the day
slides.body: The deposit alone was more than either of our first month's rent ever was.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, car insurance, phone & fibre, electricity & water, gifts, entertainment
slides.body: This is the bucket that funds every Saturday we're not looking at venues.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R36 000. Four months to go. The savings line needs to win a few more of these.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
We put both our statements into Beyond Horizon so we could see the wedding fund against everything else we're still paying for.

No bank login needed.
